## House rules for every overnight session
- **Game name (2026-10-24, user):** "Banners of the Deep: A Dungeon Master Tale", short "BOTD" (replaces Land of Lords, which clashed with an existing MMO "Lands of Lords"). Changed in game/ (HUD, skin.dmf), the launcher and the brand/build tools. The bundle is "Banners of the Deep.app", binary `BannersOfTheDeep`; "Land of Lords.app" and "Dungeon Master Remastered.app" are symlinks to it. Game-open guards: `pgrep -x 'BannersOfTheDeep|LandOfLords'`. New player-facing text uses the new name.
- **Game name (2026-10-23, user):** "Land of Lords: A Dungeon Master Tale", short "Land of Lords" (was Kin & Stone). Already changed in game/ (HUD title, start card, header, About, Welcome line, skin.dmf window title) and in the brand and build tools. Any new player-facing text uses the new name. The bundle is now "Land of Lords.app"; "Dungeon Master Remastered.app" stays as a symlink, so old script paths keep working.

- **One shared folder.** Several sessions edit `game/` at once. Edit with exact-match replacements, re-read a region
  right before editing it, never rewrite whole files, and never leave `game/` uncompilable or the HUD broken.
- **`game/Interface/remastered.html`** is shared by four sessions. Stay inside your own area (below). After every edit:
  `node --check` the extracted script blocks, and feed a model through headless Chrome with `?overlay` reading console
  errors (`tools/check_useon_hud.py` shows how). Never put `//` comments inside one-line handlers; use `/* */`.
- **Builds, app checks and real-client runs go through the lock:**
  `python3 tools/runlock.py --who <your-name> -- <command>`. Never kill another session's process.
- **Real input:** the user is asleep, so real input is safe from them, but not from each other: any run that moves the
  pointer or sends keys goes through the lock too. Bring the client window to the front before screenshots.
- **Disk:** about 17 GB free at the start. Keep captures small (PNG/JPEG stills, short clips), under
  `reports/polish-2026-10-22/<your-name>/`. Delete bulky intermediates.
- **Keep to what the user has decided** (memory files): always 3D and Village; original unit sprites and faces kept
  (another session, "Soft 64 art", is working on unit art: leave unit sprites alone); natural faceted rock, not
  cubes; sun-and-sky light, never camera darkness; no sliding units; lock/Chase camera follows without re-centring;
  the unit card stays tabbed; the player-facing name is Kin & Stone.
- **Freeze at 06:45 EDT.** Stop editing `game/` by then, write your section below, and leave it compiling. The QA
  session does the final integrated build and check after the freeze.
- Write what you changed and how you checked it in your section, with before/after images. Write requests for
  another session under **Requests**, naming that session.

- **FYI everyone editing HUD text (hud-craft, 00:06):** WebKit (the game's HUD engine) never draws text under 9 px on screen.
  At the 0.8 Auto scale (1280x720) a 10 px or 11 px label is set at **11.25 px**; headless Chrome keeps 10 px, so a label
  that just fits in a Chrome check can clip in the game. Leave ~15 % slack or size by content. Real-WebKit headless shots
  without the lock: `reports/polish-2026-10-22/hud-craft/wkshot.swift` (notes in the shared notes folder).
- [ ] for **Soft 64 art** (from qa-stability 09:00, at the user's report of a kobold missing a leg that looks whole): in
  `Icons/Remastered/Races64/*.dmi`, the limb-loss poses (`NoRightLeg`, `NoLeftLeg`, `NoLegs` and the combinations) barely
  differ from the whole body on small races: the kobold's leg pose removes only its bottom 5 rows of 64, about 3–4 pixels on
  screen. Please make a lost leg read at game scale (the whole leg gone to the hip with a clear gap, a bigger stump), kobold
  first, then goblin, frogman and the other short-legged races; arms likewise if they suffer the same. Comparison:
  `reports/polish-2026-10-22/qa-stability/limbs/small-races-leg-x3.png`. The code side is checked (`tools/check_limb_pose.py`).

- [x] for world-look (user, 11:52, relayed by hud-craft): "tell this the person doing the damage pop ups see when i zoom
  out it moves": the damage numbers move while the camera zooms out (since your 10:0x zoom-sized, unit-following
  numbers). The user's screen recording was lost (a temporary preview; nothing saved to the Desktop), so how they move is
  not known from it. Messaged world-look.
  **Done (world-look, 12:0x):**
  - Two causes. First, a number was re-sized to the zoom every frame, and its scatter and rise with it, so it slid
    against the unit while zooming. Its size is now fixed for its life when it appears; new numbers come in at the new
    zoom's size.
  - Second, the numbers were drawn with the previous frame's camera, so they lagged a frame behind any zoom, pan or
    turn. They are now drawn right after the camera is set.
  - Headless, blows landing at zoom 13 and then 12 wheel steps out to 41: the number's offset from the unit's head
    (its own rise taken out) changes by 0 px sideways and under 1 px up or down. Before: up to 4 px and 10 px, and a
    size change mid-zoom.
  **Still moving (user, 12:3x: "the popups still move when camera moves or zoomes in"). Real cause found and fixed
  (world-look, 12:45):**
  - The HUD is scaled with a CSS zoom on the whole page. In WebKit (the game's engine) the number canvas is laid out at
    the zoomed size, but its buffer was the window's size, so it was stretched.
  - At HUD scale 0.8 (a 1280×720 window) every number sat 1.25× as far from the top left as its unit: 30–228 px to the
    side and up to 88 px below, the further from the top left the worse. Moving or zooming the camera moved the units at
    1× and the numbers at 1.25×.
  - Chrome (all my headless checks) lays it out differently and was right, which is why nothing caught it.
  - The buffer is now sized from the canvas's own box, and each number (and the HUD-panel cut-outs) is mapped from the 3D
    view's on-screen box to the number canvas's box.
  - Checked in a real WKWebView by finding the drawn number's pixels: at HUD scale 0.8 it is within 0.3 px sideways of
    its unit's head (before: 30–228 px off), and scale 1 is unchanged. Chrome is unchanged at both scales.
    `check_hud_watch` passes.
## hud-craft

How I check: `reports/polish-2026-10-22/hud-craft/capture_hud.py <out>` renders every HUD state (132 scenes: each
unit-card and band-card tab, every page and sub-view both empty and with data, Log, Settings, every card and drawer,
the top-centre notices together, tooltips, the nine race materials, colour-blind mode, worst cases) over a terrain still
at the Auto HUD scale, in headless Chrome or in a real WKWebView (`--engine wk`, the game's own engine, through
`wkshot.swift`), and lists console errors, clipped text, collapsed scrollers and overlapping panels. Baseline:
`r0-before/`. My CSS is one block at the end of the stylesheet ("hud-craft polish", icons generated by `icons.py`); my
JS changes are small and marked "hud-craft". The house style is written down in `hud-craft/STYLE.md`.

**Final summary (freeze text as of 05:22; later rounds, if any, are logged below it).** Before/after in the game's own engine (WebKit, 1440x900):
`summary-before-after-webkit-1440-a.jpg`, `-b.jpg` (everyday states), `-c.jpg`, `-d.jpg` (views with data),
`-e.jpg` (the late rounds). 82 rounds, logged below.
- *What changed:*
  - One look: every panel, card, drawer, notice and message in the race material (frame, pane, accent, ink) with the
    solid pane under its texture; one icon family of 52 vector icons in place of mixed pixel icons, text glyphs and
    emoji (menu, action bar, top bar, page crests, sub-tabs, card badges, every action in the right-click menu and near
    card, workshops in Build and Work, inline status icons); the last labels on the old fixed gold now follow the race
    (elves see pale blue, the dead bone).
  - Bars: a lit fill, tenths and a damage trail; low health pulses; health strips on the band's portraits; recharge
    lines on the race special and weapon moves; the unit's warnings as chips under its bars; a red pip on the Health tab
    when a part is injured.
  - Tooltips: a short title, details and the hotkey as a keycap (from the title or the button's own key), on disabled
    controls too, always on screen.
  - Windows: one at a time, only its menu button lit, 0.12–0.14 s fades and slides, pages and drawers sized to fit,
    frames never colliding at any size from 1024x640 to 3440x1440, notices stacked (and stepping aside for the world
    map and Settings, and above a craft list), menus and cards kept on screen at every HUD scale.
  - Fit: everything legible in WebKit at 1024x640 (the 9 px text floor), Village roster rows a line shorter, the
    lineage one column, task cards with an action line, logs striped by kind, a world map legend, the top bar naming
    the level, HUD size capped to what the window holds.
  - Every control has hover, press, keyboard focus and disabled states; HUD checkboxes are drawn by the HUD; dragging
    across the HUD no longer selects its text.
  - Colour-blind mode covers every green/red cue in the panels (it left the health bar blank before).
  - Requests from playtest done: nav lighting, window piling, clipped labels, workshop icons, the vanishing minimap,
    hover names, Fortress hint, a dragon's card, near-card action labels.
  - Functionality unchanged apart from what those requests asked; no DM code touched. One data file: the Controls
    drawer's stale A/E/Q labels in `game/Interface/border-controls.json`.
- *How checked:* `capture_hud.py` in Chrome at four sizes and in real WebKit at 1024x640, 1280x720, 1440x900,
  1920x1080 and 2560x1440 (final run: 528 Chrome captures and 660 WebKit captures of the page as of 05:02, 0 console errors, 0 clipped, 0 collapsed, overlaps only the expected ones); `jump_check.py` (live updates move nothing, 0 moved); scans for text over text, text in the
  wrong colour, colliding frames, hover/press/focus states, contrast in the nine materials; `node --check` on every
  script block; the real client under the lock with real clicks (`hud_real.py`), 13 runs: 17/17, 18/18, 19/19, 20/20, 20/21, 21/21, 23/23, 24/26, 23+crash, 26/26, 26/27, 26/26, and the final page 26/26 (every miss was my runner: a click outside a list, a gap read in screen pixels, a log line cut short, a hover it can't send).
- *Still rough:* see the end of this section.

  be cut. Its look is the HUD's; its placement is rts-feel's/world-look's.
- Possible bug filed for rts-feel/qa: villager priority may run Low-first (Requests).
- Typographic marks stay as text on purpose: ✓/○ in goal lists, ★/☆ milestones, † for the dead, ♥ between partners
  in the lineage tree.
- Tooltip and message wording is playtest's; the HUD only lays it out (title, keycap, details).
- Suggestion: the top bar has no stock readout (wood, stone, food), which most RTS HUDs keep in view. The model only
  carries stock counts for the Village board view (`board.stats`), so it needs the game to send them every update (a
  few fields in HUD.dm). The bar is full at 1440x900, but its position readout repeats the coordinates on the minimap
  plate, so that slot could hold the three counters.

## world-look

### Summary at the freeze (06:05; the round-by-round log follows)

**What changed** (all in the 3D part of `game/Interface/remastered.html`, plus one equivalent read in
`Code/Remastered/View3D.dm`):
- **Speed.** Garbage per frame 5.8 → 0.67 MB at 200 units (allocation-free geometry helpers, buffers kept between
  frames); terrain built in 8x8-tile chunks joined in 32x32-tile groups, so a mined block or felled tree costs a few ms,
  not a full rebuild; unchanged terrain resends skipped; pan steps defer the rebuild and pre-build chunks a few ms a
  frame; placed objects cached; sun shadow map redrawn only when it changes; cheaper shadow filter; damage numbers on
  one canvas (they cost 8 ms a frame in WebKit fights). v3frame: 0.5–1.0 ms at 59–419 things, 1.7 ms in a 30-blows-a-
  second brawl (Chrome replay); real WebKit client: 1 ms, 60 fps (p95 19–20 ms) when the machine isn't overloaded.
- **Light.** Sun and sky colour by time of day (golden low sun, blue hour, moonlit night that keeps colours readable),
  seamless across the day/night switch; moon shadows; underground warm grade; season tints (autumn canopies, winter,
  spring); cloud shadows; meadow colour variation; a very faint vignette; firelight that flickers and glows with embers.
- **Terrain.** Shores slope into the water with a foam line, deep-to-shallow water with ripples, sky reflection and
  glints; ground darkens where it meets rock and walls; grass blade tufts; the horizon no longer goes black at night.

  crisp screen-space health bars with a draining "just lost" chip; pictures lean back in the Top camera so they read.
- **Effects.** Hit flash, blood/bone/ichor bursts, parry sparks, arrow streaks, death fade and slump, footstep dust,
  construction dust, trees swaying, snow, falling leaves, fireflies. Audio hooks: `impact`, `fall`, `built`.

### Log

How I check: `tools/worldlook_replay.py` (new). `dump` builds two scenes with the game's own code in an arena
(`tests/worldlook_dump_test.dm`: a village on grass with desert/marsh/snow patches, a pond, a forest, cactus, a rock
mountain with a tunnel, a timber house, 57 villagers of 7 races; and a dug hall underground) and writes what the 3D
view is sent. `shots` replays the real page code on that data in headless Chrome on this Mac's GPU (Metal) at fixed
cameras, no input; `WORLDLOOK_HTML=restore-points/.../remastered.html` renders the same cameras from the restore point
for before/after. `perf` clones the crowd to N units and records the CPU time of every `v3frame` and the frame
interval. Allocation numbers come from a CDP sampling heap profile (incl. collected garbage).

**Round 1 (22:45–23:00): render-loop allocations, unit shadows.** Closes the POLISH.md open item.
- The geometry helpers (`quad`, `quad4`, `tri`, `box`, `boxr`, `MD.f`, `MD.blob`) no longer make temporary arrays; the
  blob's shape is worked out once. Checked in node: identical vertex output to the old helpers over 159k values.
- Every per-frame upload goes through one reused Float32Array (`v3up`), and the frame's big buckets (sprites by
  picture, shadows, rings, bars, silhouettes, the objects bucket) are kept between frames (`VA`, a growable
  Float32Array with `.length`), written with a fixed-arity vertex call.
- Garbage per frame at 200 units: **5.8 MB → 0.66 MB**. `v3frame` CPU median: 0.8/1.3/2.2 ms → 0.4/0.4/0.5 ms at
  57/200/400 units; 60 fps throughout at 1440x900 (`perf-before.json`, `perf-r1.json`).
- Unit shadows: the six 7%-alpha discs (barely visible) are now one soft contact shadow under the feet plus, on the
  surface, the unit's own picture laid on the ground away from the sun or moon (Diablo-style), its length from the
  sun's height, its strength from the light's (`r1/morning-compare.jpg`). Underground only the contact shadow shows.

**Round 2 (23:00–23:08): light and atmosphere** (answers playtest's P1 night request).
- New `v3grade()`: sun colour/strength and sky fill by time of day (golden low sun, cool fill), a moonlit-blue night
  grade that keeps each colour's identity (grass stays dark blue-green, not grey), moon path and moon shadows (the
  shadow map now runs at night), stars fade in. Day's end and night's start meet at the same twilight values, so the
  game's night flag flips with no jump.
- Underground has its own warm, earthy grade (was purple-grey).
- Season tint on green ground and leaves only (never unit pictures): autumn toward olive/gold, winter drained and
  cool, spring fresher; eased over a few seconds when the season changes.
- A little aerial haze across the iso view. Units' pictures keep more of their colour at night.
- Before/after: `r2/grade-before-after.jpg` (night, evening, underground; left = restore point, right = now).

**Round 3 (23:08–23:14): water and shorelines.**
- Land that touches water now slopes down into it: each corner it shares with water dips below the surface (by a
  varied amount, so the shore wobbles), and the water's surface reaches under that bank, so the shore runs where the
  water meets the slope instead of along square tile edges with brown walls. Units on the bank stand on the slope.
- Water is shaded deep in the middle and sandy-teal at the shore; swamps murky green-brown. The surface has its own
  shader branch: moving ripples, the sky in it (more at a glancing look), small sun glints. No more ground-detail
  texture on water. Before/after: `r3/water-before-after.jpg`.
- Grass↔desert/marsh transitions were already blended per corner; left as they are.

**Round 4 (23:14–23:21): combat feel.** All timed to when a blow or shot *lands* (the hits feed plus the shot's flight):
- the struck unit's picture flashes warm white for ~0.12 s;
- a short burst flies off it, away from the striker: a star of light, droplets coloured by what was hit (blood; bone
  chips for skeletons; dark ichor for zombies; frogman/lizardman/vampire their own), a small splash on a kill or a big
  blow; a parry or block throws sparks instead;
- arrows, bolts and javelins leave a faint streak of light behind them in flight;
- a unit that leaves the view fades out (0.35 s) instead of popping; a killed one darkens, slumps and sinks (0.9 s).

- Additive passes (sparks, magic glows, fire halos) now fade toward black with distance instead of picking up haze.

**For audio — event hooks** (guarded `window.rmSfx&&rmSfx.at(name,x,y,info)`, tile coords):
- `impact` — the moment a blow or shot lands on a unit (hits feed time + projectile flight). `info={k,w,spark}`: k is
  the hit kind (hit/big/kill/parry/block/...), w the weapon, spark true for a parry/block. Use it if you want sounds in
  sync with arrows landing rather than with the feed.
- `fall` — a killed unit starts to slump out of view (once per death).
- `built` — a wall or building piece just finished (`info={kind}`, built/bfloor), with its dust ring.

## rts-feel

Plan: everything page-side so it answers on the next frame, layered on the existing handlers. My code is one separate
`<script>` block right after the main script in `remastered.html` (starts `/* RTS feel (overnight polish 2026-10-22,
rts-feel)`), plus four guarded one-line hooks in v3wire's mouseup/dblclick and v3frame (`rfClick`, `rfBoxFx`, `rfDbl`,
`rfDraw`). **audio:** if you add the `<!--rm-audio-->` marker after the main script, put it after my block or before it,
either is fine, but please match on `</body>` rather than `</script>\n</body>` (my block sits between them).
Sound hooks I call (guarded): `rmSfx.order(kind,{x,y,queued})` at the click with kind move|attack|gather|chop|mine|patrol
(capture → attack, pick up → gather); `rmSfx('select')`, `rmSfx('group-set')`, `rmSfx('group-recall')`, `rmSfx('deny')`
(a click that orders nothing). Tools and evidence: `tools/rts_feel/`, `reports/polish-2026-10-22/rts-feel/`.

### Summary for the morning (final, 05:41; the round-by-round log follows)
**What changed for the player.** Every click answers on the next frame (a ping where the order lands: move, attack,
dig, chop, pick up, patrol; a flash on the target; a red cross for a click nobody can carry out; gold selection rings
at once; dashed waypoint lines for Shift-queued orders) and the pointer says what a click will do (sword, pickaxe, axe,
hand, a ring under the target, the verb in the tag). Selection: click / box / Shift / double-click or Ctrl-click for
that people on screen; zoomed in, a click or a box anywhere on a body counts. Control groups on the digits (Ctrl sets,
Shift adds, twice jumps), chips above the action bar. Camera: edge scroll (Settings, with speed), smooth arrows, eased
wheel, Z, F1 or the top bar's idle count, Backspace, a local minimap to press / drag / right-click, the unit card's
portrait. Orders: the first step in the same tick and on screen ~120–170 ms after the click (was ~300); workshop
clicks walk over and open there; unreachable or blocked building sites say why; mined stone is carried; a click on a
rock ridge mines its face at once; A then Esc or right-click cancels; Esc closes an open window before it deselects; R, P, Z, digits
and friends work whichever part of the window has the keyboard; no command is lost when two are sent at once; every
action-bar hotkey shows on its button. Settings: right-click can give orders (default stays the menu; a second
right-click runs its main action). Villager priority 1 · High really goes first.
**Found and fixed on the way.** WebKit stopped reading the page at `send('ready')`, so every script after it (the sound
engine, my block) never ran in the game; the ready request is now the page's last script. WebKit dropped the first of
two commands sent in one go (now queued). Villager priority ran Low first against every label. Zoomed in, clicks on a
person's feet or head were move orders. A click on a rock ridge's top was "walk onto the peak" (a stairs / climbing
gear message) while the pointer said Mine. A late 3D update pulled the camera back after a fast edge scroll.
**How it was checked.** Real client with real input through the lock (`tools/rts_feel/real_feel.py`): **r20 32/32**
with everything in (latency, selection, groups, keys from both focuses, A/Esc, wheel, edge, minimap, verdicts,
workshop walk, zoomed-in body clicks, no runtime or page errors). `zsh tools/rts_feel/verify_all.sh` **ALL OK at 05:29 and again at 05:40** (after the last game/ edit):
hooks and block in place, ready request last, every script parses, game/ compiles, skin macro names unique, headless
Chrome suite (48 checks, 47 pass, the minimap press-and-drag one skips in Chrome, whose CSS zoom maps the pointer
differently; the real client covers it), the same page in a real WKWebView, arena tests (first step and its push,
workshop walk, check_breaking with the carried stone and the ridge click, check_settlement with priority). Also passing:
check_attack, check_qol, check_easy_orders, check_work_selection, check_halls, check_construction, check_hud_watch;
check_orders_integration 45 of 56 shards (the other 11 fail the same way on the 22:40 code, see Requests).
**Still rough** (details in `reports/polish-2026-10-22/rts-feel/README.md`): right-click is the menu by default; the
game window's letter keys are the original verbs; HUD panels show the system arrow; a key pressed while no control
has the keyboard is lost (R after the story card, Esc on a fresh question card: needs `{focus:'page'}` in the app's
WebKit bridge, a native rebuild); edge scroll pauses after 6 s of a still pointer; unreachable building spots aren't
refused at placement; climbing onto a ridge with gear still says "Mine" until the game's verdict arrives.

## audio

### Summary at the freeze (05:40) — what changed, how it was checked, what's still rough

**What changed**
- `game/Interface/audio.js` (new, ~117 KB, ASCII): a synthesizer and sound engine for the HUD page. Nothing is a recording.
  108 named sounds / 276 takes (interface, order cues with race accents, combat, magic, the 14 specials, work, building,
  goods, ambient creatures, 16 ambience beds incl. rain/thunder and a village murmur, battle drums, an arrival swell), a
  formant voice synth for 13 voices (every race mapped) x male/female x 12 line kinds x 4 takes with per-race character,
  and a generative music bed (3 moods, 2-3 progressions each, arpeggio / sparse / flute-air phrases; a phrase, then 25-70 s
  of rest; battle drums under fights).
- Engine: categories -> master -> 35 Hz high-pass + presence -> bus compressor -> make-up -> limiter; two convolution rooms
  (open air / caves, only the active one runs); world sounds panned and attenuated from the 3D camera; variety (takes,
  pitch, never the same take twice) and a start-time throttle (gap and voice count per sound, 30 in all, nearest wins,
  batches spread, crowds thicken instead of getting louder); all synthesis in a Web Worker built from the synth's own
  source; starts at load where WebKit allows (the app does), else on the first click. Main-thread cost in the real app
  ~0.06 ms per HUD update.
- Sources, with no edits in others' code: wraps updateHUD / update3D / send / logPush; document listeners; panels and body
  states; hooks the others call: rts-feel `rmSfx.order` + select / group-set / group-recall / deny, world-look
  `rmSfx.at('impact'|'fall'|'built')`. Ready-made but unused: `rmSfx.weather(...)`.
- Settings → Sound: Master, Effects, Interface, Voices, Ambience, Music (70/80/55/75/50/35) + mute in background (window
  hidden/covered, or another app in front via WebKitBridge.swift `dmAppActive`). Saved per player on the server
  (`Code/Remastered/Audio.dm`, profile key "audio"). The HUD's other localStorage settings now survive restarts too
  (profile key "hud"; the app's web view forgets page storage on quit).
- DM: `Code/Remastered/Audio.dm` (new), 5 one-line hooks in HUD.dm; the original 8-bit fight/arrow WAVs routed through
  `remaster_native_sounds = 0` (Bows.dm, Siege.dm, one line each). `mac-webview/WebKitBridge.swift` +13 lines (webview
  module rebuilt through the lock; in the current app). `tools/runlock.py`: deadlock and crash fixes.

**How it was checked** (`reports/polish-2026-10-22/audio/`, its README.md lists everything; all pass at 05:40)
- `node tools/render_audio.js`: 1389 takes render, none clips or is silent. `tools/check_audio_hud.py` (headless Chrome):
  every hook and setting, throttle, restore/mirror, no long main-thread tasks. `tools/check_audio_mix.py`: the engine's own
  chain offline — default scene -21.7 dB RMS, worst battle peak -1.3 dBFS. `tools/check_audio_webkit.py` (real

**Still rough**

### Round log

Plan: a sound engine in its own file, `game/Interface/audio.js`, inlined into the HUD page when the server sends it
(HUD.dm replaces the `<!--rm-audio-->` marker after the main script; please keep that marker). Everything is synthesized in
code (no downloads, no sample files); the same synth code renders WAVs offline for level checks. Volumes (Master, Effects,
Interface, Voices, Ambience, Music, mute in background) live in Settings and are saved in the player's profile on the server
(`units/remaster_profile_<ckey>.sav`, key "audio"), because the app's web view storage does not survive a restart.
Hook API (all guarded, harmless when audio is absent): `window.rmSfx&&rmSfx(name,opts)`, `rmSfx.order(kind,{x,y})`,
`rmSfx.at(name,x,y)`. Audio wraps `updateHUD`/`update3D` itself to read hits, notices, level-ups, z-level, night and units,
and listens to button hover/click and dialog open/close with document-level listeners, so it needs no edits in your code.

## playtest

### Summary (05:55; written for the morning)

27 rounds, 22:49 → 06:02, each a brand-new player (one returning) in the real packaged app on a private profile, real
AppKit input, rebuilt before every round so the night's fixes were checked as players get them. Every common race was
played (plus a rare Dragon), each round a different start. 107 stills in `reports/polish-2026-10-22/playtest/`
(JPEG); `r22-first-minutes-final-sheet.jpg` is the launcher → start card → race card → story → first company, as of 05:26.

**The first ten minutes now** (rounds 22–26, confirmed in the real app unless noted): a daytime key-art launcher (dwarves in their valley), hover-lit
buttons; a branded loading window that stays until the game window is up; a loading cover with a random tip; a start card
("Kin & Stone · Choose your people"); a race card with one line per people (rare draws starred and described); an arrival
story card with "First steps"; a goal tracker top left that walks the player from "Meet your company" to "Try your hand at
crafting" (that wording not yet seen in the app; the goal itself was) and then on to the next rank; a safe start (no hostiles for 10 minutes, wood in reach or carried, room in the
pack); F3 opens a Guide that reads "How to play" + a six-line Shortcuts list. No raw "{Player}" tags, no Title Case system
lines, no bogus milestones, no empty morning report. No client errors and no runtime errors in any round's logs.

**What I found, ranked by how badly it hit a new player, and where it stands**
1. Death in the first two minutes (skeleton pack wiped a company; frogmen; undead at the spawn) → qa SafeStart + grace:
   **confirmed** rounds 6–26, no start attacked since.
2. A new player was never told to pick a race; the race pick and the story were stock white OS windows with typos →
   start card, race card, story card (playtest): **confirmed** from round 2.
3. The goal path dead-ended: no room to carry a log (qa), goals never ticked from the Build tab or a craft (playtest),
   treeless/desert starts (qa moves + playtest carried-logs net), mining dropped its stone (rts-feel), the campfire stalled
   on a ledge or under one of your own units (rts-feel) → **confirmed** except the carried-logs net (random, not seen).
4. Starts inside or behind rock (pockets, cliffs) → world-look cutaway + qa sky check: **confirmed** (rounds 11–22).
5. HUD clutter: panels piling up, nav buttons stuck lit, clipped labels, vanishing minimap, raw type names → hud-craft:
   **confirmed**.
6. Controls: stale hover verbs, Z, whole-world minimap, edge scroll with the pointer outside, no walk-to-workshop, ridge
   clicks going to the top → rts-feel: **confirmed** (one small stall left, below).
7. Grey night, no Sound settings → world-look, audio: **confirmed**.
8. Wording (owner tags, tap/click, 2D/Classic/"hero frame" jargon, "What Action Will You Choose?", "Failed!", "1 people",
   dragons as "Settler") → playtest/hud-craft: **confirmed**; the tag sweep finds 0 tags in every view.

**Still rough (ranked)**
1. A start with no trees within reach can still happen (SafeStart: "no better spot nearby", round 13). My carried-logs net
   covers the first goals but was never seen in the real app (random); qa's wider search is the real fix.
2. The first Mine order on a ridge can stall ("No way through yet; trying again") until the player clicks again
   (rts-feel, round 21).
3. Native `<select>` menus (HUD size, difficulty, Village bulk jobs) are plain macOS menus; fine, but they break the
   game's look. My harness can't drive them, so they are untested by me.
4. "Lizardmen Scout/Hunter" (plural race in NPC names) and the original's combat sentences ("they drop their weapon!")
   are the original game's text, left as they are.
5. Pressing Caves over solid rock shows a blank orange plain with no hint (world-look, round 24).
6. Not covered tonight: hosting/joining, digging into the caves, a full day/season, raids, trade caravans.

### qa-stability: armour over a lost limb (user + coordinator, 09:0x–09:22)
The user, about the kobold "Yipeekki" that looked whole with a leg missing: "the armor does account for the missing

with armor needs to be in place as well", "the gaultets still shows".
- **Cause:** the body pose was right (`NoRightLeg`), but the 3D picture stacks the worn gear on it fitted to the whole
  body (`Remaster3DLayers`, View3D.dm), so greaves painted the lost leg back and a vambrace the lost arm. The original's
  2D overlays (`RebuildOverlays`, OverlayBuilds.dm) do the same; left alone, as asked.
- **Fix (3D only, `game/`):** new `Code/Remastered/LimbGear.dm` plus three hooks in View3D.dm (the layer list, the
  strip, the picture's cache key).
  - Gear over both sides (greaves, chestplate, a woman's top, shields, weapons) is cut where the limb was: the
    pixels the whole body has and the missing-limb pose doesn't, the stump (pose pixels past the old body, or blood red
    on it), and 2 px beside the limb outside the pose's body. Gear over what's left of the body is never cut.
  - A piece made for one arm (vambrace, gauntlet) isn't drawn at all once that arm is gone: where the hand hung over
    the hip, a cut alone left the gauntlet there.
  - Capes, quivers, helmets and crowns are never cut. Grafted and false limbs count as there, so their gear stays.
  - The masks are built from the race's own 64 px sheet per pose, facing and frame and cached: about 0.3 s the first
    time a race-and-pose combination appears in a server run, nothing after.
  - Earlier today, same thread: a unit missing a limb gets no 3D model (the "3D unit models" look), so its sprite shows
    the loss.

### weapon-cap: no weapon skill above Attack (user, 2026-10-23 ~12:00, from the coordinator)
The user: "weapon skill level can never go higher than the attack skill level".
- **The rule (`game/`, DM):** the eleven weapon skills on the card's Combat tab (Sword, Axe, Mace, Spear, Dagger, Bow,
  Unarmed, Claws, Shield, Armour, Throwing) are held at the unit's Attack level. `RemasterWeaponCap()`,
  `RemasterHeld()` and `RemasterHoldWeaponSkills()` in `Code/Remastered/CombatSkills.dm`; hooks in `Skills.dm`
  (`RemasterAddXP`, the skill tick's one-off-boost path, its first sight of a unit and the end of every pass, the skill
  panel).
- **XP earned at the cap (the choice): kept.** A held weapon skill's bar fills to just short of the next level and
  stops there. Training XP goes on counting (`remaster_xp`), and as soon as Attack levels, the weapon skill rises with it
  (as far as its XP reaches), with the usual "Axe level 35!" line. A one-off jump (stolen thoughts, a draught) stops at
  Attack and keeps nothing above it, so a temporary boost can't be banked.
- **Held on the blow itself (12:4x):** the original game adds a little weapon skill on every swing, block, deflect and
  shot (the cooldowns are only on weapon moves). At first the hold ran once a second on the skill tick, so a unit could
  be a fraction over Attack for up to a second. Now `RemasterHoldNow()` runs right where each gain happens: the end of
  `DamageType`, `CheckDefence` and the shield block in Combats.dm, the bow shot in Combat - Bows.dm, the stoneskin
  draught, and stolen thoughts (Interact.dm, Turfs.dm). It does what the tick would have: a swing's gain becomes kept
  XP, and a one-off jump stops at Attack. No blow ever lands with a weapon skill above Attack.
- **Existing units and saves:** the first time the skill tick sees a unit (so after every load), a weapon skill above
  Attack is held at Attack with its XP kept. Nothing is lost: raise Attack and it comes back. There are no messages for
  this. The card shows the held value even before that first tick.
- **New units:** Attack is now seeded from the best of all eleven weapon skills (before: the melee ones only), so a new
  unit with Bow, Shield or Armour above its melee skills keeps them. Strength is still seeded from melee.
- **Two knock-on fixes:**
  - **Crown** (`Items/Crowning.dm`, one hook; `RemasterCrownHealth`, CombatSkills.dm). The user (12:3x), on my first
    version (+25 Attack to go with the crown's +25 weapon skills): "no +25 crowning rule maybe more health?". So the
    crown no longer touches weapon skills or Attack. It gives +150 health (HP and max HP; it was +100), plus its old
    +10 Strength, +10 Agility and +40 Sneaking. The amount is `RM_CROWN_HEALTH`. The user settled on +150 (12:5x),
    after talking through a Rule skill for rulers (levels 1–10, a health bonus for people nearby): "lets just keep
    crown at 150+ and thats that we will think more in the future". I'd started that skill and took it out again;
    none of it is left in `game/`.
    - **The user's rulership ideas, for a design later (not built):** crowning should differ by the settlement's stage
      (Camp → Kingdom, `rm_ranks` in Progress.dm); the player picks what the leader is called ("all the leader or crown
      tags"); becoming ruler should need ruler items crafted from gold and other materials; and there should be
      different kinds of succession and ruler items. Today any stage can Declare Leader without an item (the Bone and
      Gold Crowns are optional), the title is always King or Queen, and Town renames them Lord or Lady.
      Design draft with open questions: `planning/RULERSHIP.md` (nothing built).
    - Stepping down takes off exactly what the crown gave (`rm_crown_health`), and never takes health below 1. Before,
      a hurt ruler could die of stepping down.
    - A ruler crowned the old way, before today, keeps its +25 weapon skills (held at Attack) until it steps down. Then
      the old +100 health and the +25s come off its real levels.
    - A ruler born royal can't be told apart from one crowned the old way, so nothing converts old rulers on load.
  - **Stoneskin draught** (`Remastered/Brewing.dm`): when it wears off, Armour never drops below where it was. If the +15
    had been held at Attack, the old `-= gain` would have cost 15 real levels.
- **Not held:** creatures and NPCs nobody owns (their combat skills are never seeded, so their Attack is the default
  1), and a weapon a race never learnt (Bow 0) stays at 0.
- **Card** (`remastered.html`, tooltips only, no new CSS): a weapon tile at its Attack level gets `data-cap`, and its
  tooltip reads "Axe level 30 / 14,818 XP (+100,045 kept) / Held at Attack level 30: train Attack to raise it". The
  Character panel's sub-skills say "… · held at Attack level 30 · …", and Attack's skill guide gets one more line.
  hud-craft: `data-cap` is there if a held tile should look different. Still (headless Chrome, a made-up unit):
  `reports/polish-2026-10-22/weapon-cap/combat-tab-held-axe-tooltip.png`.
- **Checked:**
  - New `tools/check_weapon_cap.py` (`tests/weapon_cap_test.dm`, an arena on the shared engine; about 4 min, because the
    draught wears off after 3): all 29 checks pass (`tests/weapon-cap-checks.json`; three are "held at once", before any skill tick: a real blow, a jump, the draught). It covers seeding; training and direct XP at the cap (level held, XP kept);
    Attack 35 lifting a held Axe, with the level line; a one-off jump stopping at Attack; all eleven held; an old save
    written and read back the game's way (the player's `Write`/`Read`, as SaveUnits/LoadUnits do), with Bow 40 and
    Sword 25 over Attack 10 held, their XP kept, no messages, the card held before the first tick, and both back once
    Attack is 45; crowning (+150 health, skills unchanged) and stepping down, even when hurt, plus a ruler crowned the old way; the draught held, then wearing
    off back to 30 (not 15); unowned creatures not held; Bow 0 staying 0; the HUD fields.
  - `check_combat_skills`: passes (Attack is still seeded at 40 from Sword 40, Armour 30, Bow 20).
  - `check_skills`: the "boost" line now raises Attack to 50 first, so its Sword +25 isn't held (test updated). Three

    record: they expect unpaced woodcutting XP, and it's paced by level now. `tools warned` still counts warnings per
    unit, but since `Tools.dm`'s 05:51 change they're kept on the player. Those tests need updating by their owners.
  - **Fixture fix (13:0x, reported by hud-craft):** `tests/moves_native_probe.dm` gave the Pyromancer Sword 25 and no
    Attack, so with the hold its Fire wave, Lunge and Heavy blow showed locked and `check_moves_input` timed out. Its

### rulership: seats by stage, regalia, titles, laws, the heir's item (user, 2026-10-23 afternoon, from the coordinator)
The user, on the draft `planning/RULERSHIP.md`: "build it in game"; titles from a list only, no typing your own; and
"the heir holds an item too": it can be stolen, succession honours who holds the items, so killing a prince or
princess and taking the item can take the succession and the realm. The draft now records those decisions, the
claim design (section 5) and what stays open.
- **What changed (`game/`, DM):** new `Code/Remastered/Rulership.dm` (included last in the .dme), with small hooks:
  `AddLeader`/`RemoveLeader` (Items/Crowning.dm), the crown's place in `EquipItem` (Items/Item Procs.dm, one line),
  `RemasterCrownHealth` (CombatSkills.dm), `RemasterHeirOf`/`RemasterSuccession`/`RemasterCanInherit`
  (Succession.dm), the Kingdom's need and the rank-up (Progress.dm), `RemasterSetName` (Names.dm), the rename
  (SelectedActions.dm), the Realm page's commands and a house rename (Realms.dm), peace and a fallen realm (War.dm).
  - **A seat per stage.** Declare Leader (and putting regalia on) crowns only a unit holding the stage's regalia or
    better: Chief's Totem or the old Bone Crown (Camp), Elder's Staff, Chain of Office, Silver Circlet, Gold Crown
    (Kingdom). Health by stage, as far as the regalia worn reaches: +50, 75, 100, 125, 150 (`rm_seat_health`; the
    Kingdom's is `RM_CROWN_HEALTH`). No weapon skills or Attack. Regalia off: the seat stays, the bonus goes; on again,
    it's back. A rising stage keeps the old title and bonus until the next item is worn, and the Realm page says
    what's needed. The Kingdom needs "a ruler wearing the Gold Crown" (was "a crowned ruler").
  - **Regalia are crafted** with Craft new gear › (material) › **Regalia**: totem at the carpentry (2 wood, 1 bones),
    staff at the leatherworks (2 wood, 1 skin), chain (3 iron ingots), silver circlet (2 silver, a cut emerald), Gold
    Crown (3 gold, a cut ruby) at the forge; the heir's circlet (forge, 1 silver) and band (bone crafter, bones and
    skin). They're kept out of the generated `rm_gear_defs` (tests/gear_test.dm checks every entry there for 64 px
    pictures) and go into the workshops' lists at start. Regalia never fade on the ground. **Pictures are
    placeholders:** the two crown sprites tinted (`game/Icons/Remastered/Regalia.dmi` from
    `art/regalia/make_regalia_icons.py`).
  - **Titles** from a list per race and stage (Human, Dwarf, Orc, Goblin, Elf, Lizardman, Kobold; others use the
    Human list), asked on the HUD ask card when crowned, with the house's last title first. A pair gives the form for
    the gender (Lord/Lady). A stage rise asks again once the regalia reaches it ("Keep Elder" first). Names read
    "[Title] {House} Name"; a rename and a house rename keep the title in front (the house rename used to leave a
    ruler's old house tag).
  - **Laws of succession** (Bloodline, Chosen heir, Might, Council, Regalia), asked at the realm's first crowning
    with its race's law first; changed on the Realm page at mood -10 for 7 days. Might and Council take grown units
    only; no law takes a captive or a slave.
  - **The heir's item.** Becomes the realm's when one of its people puts it on; one per realm while it exists. Whoever
    of the realm holds it (grown, free) is the heir under every law. Stolen by killing the holder (it drops), by
    capturing them (the captor takes it with the weapons), or handed over. **Claims:** when the seat falls empty
    (the last ruler dies or steps down) and another realm's unit holds the item, that player has a claim; no one can
    be crowned meanwhile. Pressed within 10 minutes from the Realm page; the claimed realm **Yields** (becomes the
    claimant's vassal, the item is spent) or **Refuses** (war at once). It ends when the item is taken back (void),
    the holder loses it (lapses), peace is sworn (dropped, item spent), the claim isn't pressed in time (lapses, item
    spent), or the claimant takes the refusing realm's last banner (it becomes the claimant's vassal instead of only
    suing for peace). Members and vassals of one realm never claim each other's seats.
  - **Old saves:** a ruler crowned before keeps the seat, the title and whatever health they had (no regalia needed;
    the card asks for it). A name the old Town rank-up wrote as "{House} Lord Grak" is put back as "Lord {House}
    Grak". Bound items, laws and claims are saved.
- **HUD** (`remastered.html`, existing classes only, no new CSS): the unit card's Family tab shows the seat (title,
  regalia, health, what the stage needs), the heir and why ("Prince · heir: holds the Heir's Circlet"), what
  crowning would need, and another realm's item held. The Realm page has a **Rule** box (rulers, a claim on us with
  Yield / Refuse, our claims with Press the claim, the heir and where the heir's item is, the five laws with the
  current one pressed). The succession banner says when the seat is claimed and offers the Realm page instead of
  "Crown as". Stills: `reports/polish-2026-10-22/rulership/`.
- **Checked:**

  - `tools/check_rulership_hud.py` (headless Chrome, a made-up model): 8 of 8, no script errors

  - `check_hud_watch --label rulership --port 12379`: passes, 7 of 7 (`tests/rulership-checks.json`).
  - Neighbours, all pass: `check_weapon_cap` 29/29, `check_heirs`, `check_progress`, `check_curated_actions`,

  up to 230). A trace is near invisible (puffs under 3 % opacity are skipped); a thick cloud reaches 0.6. Before, every
  tile was at least 0.2, so many thin tiles stacked into a field-wide haze.

### world-look: fog of war (user, 19:5x; notes §8)
**Built (20:4x; in the app built 20:38, `Land of Lords.app`, opened for the user):**
- **Sight is a soft circle round each source.** The user (20:1x) chose "more like a circle, like the mist" over line
  of sight, which was also costly here, so rock does not block sight.
  - 12 tiles for a unit; +3 on the sky level (wall walk, tower, mountain top); +3 flying; −3 at night except Dwarf,
    Goblin, Kobold, Orc, Vampire, Spider and Dragon (my pick, change `rm_fog_dark_sight`); 0 when blind.
  - Workshops see 4, and allies share sight.
  - Surface and sky level only; underground keeps its line of sight.
- **Server (`Fog.dm`, new):**
  - Sources are bucketed in 16×16 cells each tick; "is this tile in sight" is a few circle tests, cached per tick.
  - Other players' units, NPCs and animals out of sight are not sent: `Remaster3DThings`, the moves push, and the
    far figures (which already used 7-tile sight). Loose items and effects out of sight aren't sent either.
  - Buildings once seen stay drawn where they were last seen (`rm_fog_mem`, saved with the player), marked `mem`,
    greyed and not clickable, until seen again.

  - Attacks (Attack.dm hook): a target that leaves sight is chased to its last seen spot, then the attack stops (an
    attack-move carries on).
  - Host setting "Fog of war": on by default, saved with the world (WorldSave.dm `Fog`), in Settings for the host
    only. The armour showcase switches it off.
- **Page:**
  - The server sends the area's explored bits (only when they change) plus the sight circles. The page stamps the
    circles itself, each following its unit's live position, with a 2.5-tile soft edge, into a small texture that
    the shader turns into the look.
  - The look: in sight as is; explored greyed and darker under a light mist; never seen a dim blue-grey drifting
    mist. It eases as sight changes. The far land counts as explored and the horizon as never seen; your own units
    are never dimmed (they're always in sight).
  - The minimap shows the same three states.

### world-look: GPU unit drawing (coordinator's task, 2026-10-24, the user: "3D world look: GPU unit drawing")
**Built** (`game/Interface/remastered.html` only; restore point `restore-points/page-before-gpu-units-20261024/`):
- **Instanced records.** A unit's picture, cast shadow, contact shadow and ring are one 12-number record each (a VA row:
  i0, i1, colour). The vertex shader builds the corners (an `inst` branch in the one program: 1 picture, 2 cast shadow,
  3 flat quad, 4 a ring's arc), drawn with `ANGLE_instanced_arrays` (`v3drawInst`; one draw a sheet). Without the
  extension, `v3instTris` spreads the records into triangles in JS with the same corners.
  - Rings, whole or a health arc, are one draw of arc records in the old order, since their blending is
    order-dependent.
  - The silhouette pass uses the picture records.
  - Beasts' shadows, hit flashes and magic-item effects stay triangles as before.
- **Only changed units worked out.** A standing unit's records are kept on its display entry (`kd.rc`, one reusable
  buffer, `v3rcMake`) and given back the next frame (`v3rcEmit`). They are kept while nothing they depend on changes:
  - the unit's own fields: tile, facing, selection, health, action, kind, sheet, side, size;
  - the frame's key: camera turn and tilt, the sun, terrain, settings, any new hit.
  Anything animating is never kept: walking, fighting, working, flying, drunk, growing in, a health trail, a flash.
- **Small cuts.**
  - Colours parsed once (`v3rgba`); `v3face` and the ring colours make no arrays.
  - The rock fade's nearest units picked in one pass (`v3nearest8`), not by sorting every unit of yours every frame.

**Measured** (`tools/check_unit_frames.py frames`): N units over the 3D window, the full update3D (JSON) every 0.5 s,
paced at 60 Hz. CPU ms per frame (v3frame): median / p95 / worst, then frames over 16.7 ms out of 480. WebKit's clock
ticks in whole ms.

| | 200 | 2,000 | 10,000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| WKWebView before, 20% stepping | 1 / 2 / 3 | 6 / 7 / 12 | 27 / 32 / 54, 480 over |
| WKWebView now, 20% stepping | 1 / 1 / 2 | 3 / 3 / 9 | **12 / 16 / 22**, 19 over |
| WKWebView before, standing | | 5 / 6 / 13 | 25 / 28 / 34, 480 over |
| WKWebView now, standing | | 2 / 2 / 6 | **7 / 10 / 18**, 1 over |
| Chrome before, 20% stepping | 0.9 / 1.4 / 2.4 | 3.2 / 5.5 / 8.8 | 15.7 / 17.2 / 43.4, 57 over |
| Chrome now, 20% stepping | 0.6 / 0.8 / 2.2 | 1.6 / 2.8 / 6.0 | **6.1 / 7.1 / 26.5**, 3 over |
| Chrome before / now, standing | | | 14.7 / 16.8 / 21.4, 25 over -> **5.0 / 5.6 / 20.3**, 1 over |

- Chrome's figures include ~1.5 ms of the replay page's own frame wrapper at 10,000 (performance.memory). WebKit's
  don't.
- update3D (the server's JSON, every 0.5 s) is unchanged: 1 / 2 / 9 ms at 200 / 2,000 / 10,000. That is the next
  cost at 10,000.

**Proof the look is unchanged:**
- `tools/check_unit_frames.py geometry` PASS: six scenes (village, zoomed out, night, beasts, forest, top-down) with
  hurt, selected and enemy units. The old page's triangles for every unit's picture, silhouette, cast and contact shadow
  and ring (1,599 ring triangles in the village, health arcs included) equal the new records spread into triangles. The
  third frame comes from the record cache.
- In one page, the same frame drawn with the GPU building the corners and with JS building them differs only at the
  frame-to-frame noise floor.
- The 25 fixed-camera stills are within same-page noise. `check_rock_fade.py --only clicks` PASS: a click on a unit
  picks it, clicks on faded rock or trees go through, rock and trees away still pick.
- **Real client, one short look** (arena-first rule; `check_worldlook_native.py`, 201 villagers, instanced):

### world-look: shared world sight, steps A and C (user, 2026-10-24: "merge on join, each keeps everything at war. Start step A ... then C"; plan `planning/WORLD_SIGHT_PLAN.md`)
**Built** (`game/Code/Remastered/Fog.dm`, one line in `Explore.dm`; restore point `restore-points/fog-before-sides-20261024/`):
- **A, a side's sight built once.** A side is everyone sharing sight: one alliance root (`RemasterRootKey`), and a player
  alone is a side of one (`/datum/rm_fog_side`, `rm_fog_sides`). The first member whose 3D tick comes builds its circles
  and cells (`RmFogBuildSide`). The others reuse them while they are younger than one track period (`RM_FOG_SHARE` =
  `REMASTER_TRACK_DELAY`, 5 ticks). A member's `rm_fog_circles`, cells, near and ask are the side's lists. Circles carry
  their owner, so the page still gets the follow-ref only for your own units.
- **C, one seen-before memory per side.** While allied, every member's `remaster_explored` and `rm_fog_mem` are the
  side's one map and one list (`RmFogSideMemory`):
  - a circle is marked once for the side, and everyone's map redraws (`RmFogExploredNew`, which Explore.dm's unit view
    calls too);
  - joining OR-merges what you had seen;
  - leaving or war gives you a full copy, before the side marks again;
  - each save holds the whole map, and on load the side forms again by merging. The save format is unchanged.
- **Proof** (arena, `tools/check_arena.py`):
  - `tests/fog_sides_check.dm`: the old code copied beside the new. Sides of 1, 2, 5 and 10 match it on 216,000 tile
    looks a round, on what the page is sent, and on the explored maps. On their own clocks, members reused a side 164
    times against 52 builds, never older than 4 ticks. A leaver gets their own sight. Cost for 10 players and 200 units:
    **6 ms a round each building its own, 1 ms each side once**.
  - `tests/fog_memory_check.dm`, 7/7: merge on join (buildings too), marked once (1 mark, not 3), one member's
    exploring redraws all, leaving keeps a full copy, nothing leaks either way after a split, joining again merges
    again, saves form the side again.
  - `tools/check_fog.py` 15/15, and `tests/fog_savers_check.dm` passes.

## Formations

Session "formations" (started 08:4x from the coordinator; the user's words: "the other big thing you need to delegate is
formations or unit arrival on click"). Goal: ordering a group to a spot feels like StarCraft. Areas: `Orders.dm`
`RemasterFormation` / `RemasterLevelSlots` / the slot hand-out in `RemasterOrder`, a new `Code/Remastered/Formations.dm`,
attack-move goals in `Attack.dm`, my own script block in `remastered.html` for the slot markers. I stay out of rts-feel's
mining lines (`Orders.dm` ~704–732, `Breaking.dm`, `rfMineMark`) and world-look's camera and shader.

### What's wrong today (observed 08:45, arena `tests/formation_feel_test.dm`, six units: Human, Dwarf, Goblin, Orc, Kobold, Lizardman)

Per-tick positions logged for each unit; the server's order tick at its real cadence (every 5 ticks).

| Scenario | Arrival spread | Strung out | Steps away from slot | Routes crossing | Final shape |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open ground, 17 tiles | 2.5 s | 6 tiles | 1 | 0 | the 3×2 block, kept |
| Forest | 5.0 s | 7 | 2 | 6 pairs | ragged |
| Beside a river | 1.5 s | 5 | 0 | 2 | hugs the bank; nobody sent across (good) |
| Through a one-tile doorway | **14.5 s** | **17** | **34** (three units 36–39 steps for 11 tiles) | 0 | block, in the end |
| Up stairs onto a mountain top | 3.0 s | 6 | 0 | 6 pairs | ragged cluster |
| 12 units, open ground | 3.5 s | 12 | 1 | 0 | **two holes; 2 units never got in** |
| Shift-queued second leg | 2.5 s | 7 | 7 | 0 | block |
| Attack-move | n/a | 9 | 0 | n/a | **all six crowd one tile** |

1. **Speed: every race walks at the same 2 tiles/s.** An ordered unit gets its next path tile only on the 0.5 s order
   tick (`RemasterOrdersTick` via `RemasterTrack`, every 5 ticks), so a Delay-4 unit (most races) steps every 5 ticks,
   and Delay 3 (spiders, werewolves, level-10 goblins) or a run is no faster. Only units slower than 5 ticks a step
   (gargoyles at 5 tie; slowed, crippled, wagons, siege) fall behind. So "together" is an accident of the tick.
2. **Interior units start late and get shut out.** The path search treats every unit as a wall, so a unit with
   friends on all eight sides finds no path at the click, waits for the 3 s retry, leaves last, and finds its slot (an
   inner one) already ringed by the others: in the 12-unit run two units ended "Got as close as it could" beside two
   empty slots.
3. **Jams and circling.** When the next tile of a unit's path holds a friend, `RemasterApproach` re-plans round them at
   once; in a doorway everyone re-plans round everyone every tick, so units walk away and back (34 steps away from
   their slots) and the last one arrives 14.5 s after the first.
4. **Slots are handed out nearest-unit-first, not by geometry**, so routes cross (6 pairs in the forest and on the
   mountain): units weave through each other on the way. `keep` scales the group's offsets and rounds them, so two
   units can map to one tile and the second takes "the nearest free tile" (ragged edges near trees).
5. **Facing:** `keep` keeps the old shape as it was on the map (fine, StarCraft does the same); `line`/`box` face from
   the group to the target, but on a diagonal the rounded offsets land in a staircase with gaps.
6. **Attack-move has no formation:** every unit's goal is the clicked tile and it stops within one tile of it, so the
   group arrives as a clump. Shift-queued moves compute the second leg from where the units stand at the click (not
   from the first leg's end).
7. **What the player sees at the click:** rts-feel's green ping at the clicked tile at once, the order sound, then
   (within 0.5 s, the next HUD model) a green outlined square on each selected unit's target with a line to it. The
   squares vanish the instant each unit arrives. Nothing shows where each unit will stand until the HUD model comes in.
8. **Cost:** one move order for N units on open ground: 2 → 44 ms, 6 → 67 ms, 12 → 100 ms, 25 → 183 ms, 50 → **275 ms**
   of server time in the click's tick (the tick is 100 ms). Almost all of it is the per-unit A* (`RemasterOrderPath`:
   an open-list scan per pop and `in closed` on a plain list), run for every unit in the same tick.
9. **No shuffle once there:** 0 steps after arrival in every run, 0 swaps; Bump.dm's random side-step only fires on
   things that are not the unit's next tile, so arrived units stay put. (Good; keep it.)
10. **Drag to set facing:** right-drag pans the camera, left-drag box-selects, Alt-drag turns it: no free drag gesture.
    Facing will follow the direction of travel, as in StarCraft.

### Plan (building now)
- One group per click (`datum/remaster_group`): its members, slots, facing and pace.
- Slots: a compact shape built in the direction of travel (keep = the group's own offsets, tidied onto distinct tiles;
  line / column / box snapped to the grid, clean on diagonals), legal tiles only, reachable from the group's side
  (never across water or a wall), assigned by geometry so no two routes cross (pairwise uncrossing).
- Paths go through group-mates who are still walking; a unit whose next tile holds a walking group-mate waits
  (retries next tick) instead of re-planning; after a short wait it re-plans. A unit whose slot is taken or shut in
  takes the next nearest free tile it can reach, once (no circling).
- Each step chains to the next path tile at once, so units walk at their own speed; a group that starts together
  marches at its slowest member's pace. A unit's "Own pace" switch (band card Orders tab, unit card) turns that off.
- Attack-move and Shift-queued moves get formation slots too (a queued leg starts from the previous leg's slots).
- Path searches spread over ticks for big groups, and the A* bookkeeping made O(1), to keep 50 units under a tick.
- Slot markers: my own script block draws a small marker on every unit's slot on the click's next frame (the page
  predicts the shape; the server's slots replace it a moment later) and fades each one as its unit arrives.

### What changed (in game/ since 09:20; not in a build yet)
- **New `Code/Remastered/Formations.dm`** (included last in the .dme). One click = one group: its members, slots,
  facing and pace.
  - **Slots:** `keep` moves the group's own shape over whole tiles when it is close together, and makes a block facing
    the way they go when it is spread out. `line` / `column` / `box` are built across and behind the direction of
    travel, snapped to the grid, so a diagonal line is clean. Only open tiles reachable from the target's open side
    (a flood fill through the group's own units), so never across water or a wall. Up against an obstacle the shape
    slides back toward the group until it fits. Each point takes the free tile nearest it, middle first. Slots are
    handed out by geometry (front units to the front row), then any pair whose straight routes are shorter swapped
    is swapped, so no routes cross. Each unit must be able to stand on its own tile (holy ground, flyers).
  - **On the way:** routes go through group-mates still walking. A unit whose next tile holds a walking mate waits and
    tries again the next tick (a queue at a door moves up the tick the one ahead steps); only a mate that has stood
    still 1.5 s is gone round, and when there is no way round (a doorway) it keeps waiting in line. A compact group
    plans one route and the others follow it side by side; other searches are capped at 16 a tick, and units past the
    cap step straight toward their slot and plan the next tick.
  - **Speed:** after each step a player's Move order (and an attack-move) goes straight on to its route's next tile,
    so a unit walks at its own speed (Delay), not the 0.5 s order tick. Those that set off together (within 10 tiles
    of the group's middle) march at the slowest one's pace. A unit set to **Own pace** keeps its own speed and goes
    round a slower mate in its way. Work walks and villagers' automatic orders keep the old rhythm. **Note:** most races
    are Delay 4, so a group move is now 2.5 tiles/s instead of 2 (the original game's speed); say if you want the old
    pace back.
  - **Arrival:** a unit whose slot is taken (by something that won't move off it) or shut in takes the nearest free
    tile it can reach, at most twice, so no circling. Nothing moves once there (0 steps after arrival, 0 swaps).
  - **Shift-queued moves** start their shape from the previous leg's slots. **Attack-move** gets formation slots and
    stops on its slot (it was one tile for everyone), takes its first step in the click's tick, and fights on the way
    as before.
  - The slots go to the page at once (`rmSlots3D`), and again if one changes.
- **Hooks in shared code** (small, exact-match; rts-feel told in Requests): Orders.dm (`Move` → `RemasterChainStep`,
  `RemasterApproach` → `RemasterGroupApproach` for group moves, `RemasterWalkable` skips the group's walkers in
  `rm_path_pass`, `RemasterOrderPath` bookkeeping O(1) with the same routes, `RemasterOrder` tags the group,
  `RemasterFormation` → `RemasterGroupForm`). Attack.dm: attack-move slots. HUD.dm: the `unitpace` command.
  `RemasterStepDelay`, `Bump` and `RemasterUnitData` are overridden with `..()`. New saved unit var
  `remaster_own_pace`.
- **Page, my own block** (`tools/formations/fm_module.js`, put in by `tools/formations/patch_page.py` before the ready
  script). At a move or attack-move click with 2+ selected, it works out the slots itself, porting the game's rules,
  and draws **the order queue's own square** on each on the next frame (green for a move, red for an attack-move). The
  same squares used to come only with the next HUD model, up to 0.5 s later. The game's slots replace the guess about
  0.1 s later; a square that differs glides there. Each square shrinks away as its unit stands on it. Shift keeps the
  earlier leg's squares; any other order removes a unit's square. While a group slot has its square, the order queue
  doesn't draw a second one on top; the line from the unit still runs there. It wraps rts-feel's `rfClick` / `rfDraw`
  / `rfQueueDig` without editing them. (A chevron pointing the way of travel came first; **the user prefers the
  square, 09:58**, so it's the square.)
- **Controls:** band card → Orders tab: a **Pace** row (Together / Own pace) under Formation. Unit card → Combat tab:
  a **March** row (With the group / Own pace).
- **Anchored on the click** (the user, via the coordinator, 10:2x: "they should be moving on click location as well
  not around the clicker marker"). Someone always stands on the clicked tile:
  - keep: the unit nearest the group's middle, the rest round it as they stood;
  - line: the front row's middle; column: its head; box: its middle;
  - your own formation: its gold square, or the square nearest it when that one is left empty.
  - A single unit goes to the tile itself (as before). Only a click on something nobody can stand on (a tree, rock,
    water), or a target pressed against a wall, moves the shape off the tile: then it sits on the open side.
- **What the old code did** (from the 08:45 baseline runs, `tests/formation_feel_test.dm` on the old `Orders.dm`): the
  slot search itself didn't push units outward; a compact six had a unit on the clicked tile. "Around the marker" came

  - **Attack-move:** every unit's goal was the clicked tile and each stopped within one tile of it: six in a ring

  - **Bigger groups:** the interior units found no path at the click (friends count as walls), left 3 s late and were

  - **A click on something you can't stand on:** the slots go round it, as they still do now.

- **Your own formations, with roles (Army › Formations; the user, 10:2x: "make our own army formations, like ranged units

    - a bow → Ranged;
    - a caster (`MagicalAptitude`, or a held weapon with mana) → Mage;

  | | keep formation | box |
  |---|---|---|
  | 12:52, before | 88 ms (forming alone) | |
  | today's engine, DM only (14:19) | 15 ms | 17.7 ms |
  | with the version-4 engine (15:07) | **8.8 ms avg** (7–11) | **7.8 ms avg** (6–10) |
  - In DM (`Formations.dm`, works on any engine): a stable merge sort (`RmSortBy`), slots handed out row by row along
    the formation's facing (`RemasterSnapDir`, `RemasterShapePer`), the all-pairs uncrossing pass skipped above 60
    units (`RM_SWAP_ALL`; the row-by-row hand-out leaves few crossings to undo), and the first tick of each unit's
    order spread: 2 at once, then 24 a tick on the next ticks (`RmFirstTick`).

    places), `rm_slot_tiles` (each slot's tile), `rm_sort_by`. Each replaces a DM body of the same name, so an older
    engine runs the DM (`RemasterSlotReachDM`, `RemasterSlotTilesDM`, `RmSortByDM`); `RM_NATIVE_SLOTS=0` in the
    server's environment turns them off.

  duty, not for attack orders or a monster's chase. So a fighter could step onto its foe's tile; from then on neither
  could strike (traced: `dist=0`, the swing count frozen for 2.5 minutes while healing topped both up). New
