### rts-feel: unit movement smoothness (user, 20:1x: "sometimes it glitches or lags and not smooth all the way through")
Measured (20:30), before changing anything: a server arena (`tools/rts_feel/move/move_probe.dm` in check_breaking's
arena) logs when each unit steps and what the 3D pushes would carry; `tools/rts_feel/move/sim.py` runs the page's own
glide rule on that at 60 fps. Scenes: one unit 30 tiles on open ground; through a forest and round a wall; groups of 6
and 30 in formation; a unit walking to a dig; a unit walking past six fighting.
- Server: steps are regular in every scene (Delay-4 Humans every 5 ticks; the dig walk 4–5; the fight doesn't
  disturb it; no formation waits seen).
- Pushes: `move3D` goes out every 2 ticks, so the page sees a 5-tick step as 4, 6, 4, 6 ticks.
- Glide: each tile's glide lasts the time since the last change it saw (0.4 or 0.6 s against a real 0.5 s), so a unit
  reaches its tile and waits, then rushes. Result: 10–15 pauses on every 30-tile walk, up to 0.48 s each, speed varying
  ±23–41 %.
Fix (in progress, two halves):
- Server: pushes every tick, each row carrying the unit's real step gap in ms (game speed included). The first step
  after standing takes the unit's own step time.
- Page: the glide lasts that gap.
Simulated with it: 0 pauses in every scene; speed spread 0–1 % on straight walks (forest 17 % and the dig walk 10 % are
real: diagonal steps, a 4/5-tick mix).
**world-look:** two exact-match edits in View3D.dm's moves push (`REMASTER_3D_MOVES_EVERY` 2 → 1, a 5th `move3D` row
field), plus one guarded hook in the frame loop's glide line. Not your fog or `Remaster3DThings`; told by message.
**formations:** no change to your wait rule (no waits showed up as hitches).
**In the app:** both halves are in `Land of Lords.app` (built 20:38, rebuilt 20:42): its page matches game/'s and its world
has the step-gap code. Real-client before/after runs stopped at the user's word (20:5x: "run the code and i will play
test it"); the user is playtesting the open window. `tools/rts_feel/move/track_rec.py` (new, unused for now) follows
selection rings in a screen recording frame by frame.

## Server cost (server-cost, from 21:20; coordinator's ask after the user's "lag and units that stop")
Owns: the server's per-tick code cost. Not the GC setting (coordinator: workstation GC in mac-app/launch.zsh since
22:1x) and not the app build. Notes: side-session-notes `server-cost-notes.md`.

### How the server ticks (read from the engine source)
- The DM tick is **10 a second (100 ms)**, not 30: `net.tickrate 30` is overridden when the world loads, by the world's
  default `tick_lag = 1` (OpenDream `DreamObjectWorld.SetTicklag`). `RemasterTrack` runs every 5 ticks (0.5 s) per
  player, all its work in one tick; the 3D moves push every tick.
- "MainLoop: Cannot keep up!" (RobustToolbox `GameLoop.cs`) means the loop is **more than 5 ticks (0.5 s) behind**, and
  is printed **at most once per 15 s**. The user's game 21:03–21:51: 74 of them.

### Tools (new; nothing changes in play)
- `game/Code/Remastered/TickProfile.dm`, included last: wrapper overrides time the track and its parts, the HUD model
  and its big parts, the 3D scene and its parts (terrain, things, far, fog, first-sight pictures), the moves push,
  every creature's Move and walk loop, the NPC look-rounds. Only with `RM_TICK_PROFILE=1` in the server's environment;
  then one line a game second in `tick-profile.log` (world.cpu, real time against ticks, gaps of 0.3 s or more).
- `tools/tick_profile.py`: a temp copy of game/ plus the user's saves (read only, hashes checked unchanged), the
  app's own runtime (copied), workstation GC as the app now runs. `--client real` logs the app's WebKit client in as
  the user; `--units N`, `--orders S`, `--pan N` (camera into unseen land), `--extra fixture.dm`. Reports in
  `reports/server-cost/<label>.md/.json`, with the server's physical footprint (vmmap) every 30 s.

### Baseline 1: the user's world, nobody logged in (22:1x, `reports/server-cost/none-base.md`, 10 min)
753 creatures. The DM part of a tick averages 16 ms of 100, but **94 ticks ran over 100 ms (worst 1.67 s)**, the
server fell **27 s behind in 10 min**, **25 "Cannot keep up"**. Footprint 3.0 → 3.5 GB.

| what (whole world, per game second) | ms per s | calls per s | ms per call | slowest call |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **wall-walk pass** (WallWalks.dm, every 3 s, world-wide) | ~53 avg, **100–1100 per pass** | 0.33 | ~160 | 1100 |
| NPC look for a target (`LocateTarget`, oview 5 per step) | 26.8 | 667 | 0.04 | (1585, one call: a pause landed in it) |
| creature moves (every creature's `Move`) | 23.8 | 521 | 0.05 | 13 |
| NPC look for gear (`FindGear`, view 1 per step) | 8.9 | 537 | 0.02 | 20 |
| everything else in DM (creature loops, world loops, map update) | ~87 | | | |

**The wall-walk pass is the stall.** Its ticks come exactly every 30 ticks, and **88 % of the time behind (23.9 of
27 s) falls in those seconds**. Each pass checks 40 walls; for every open side `RemasterWallOuter` floods up to 3000
tiles (`RemasterRegionLeaks`), and `RemasterWallFree` floods again: up to a dozen 3000-tile floods per wall, mostly the
map's NPC-town walls, with nobody near.

### Baseline 2: per player, 30 and 200 units (`tools/stress_timing.py`, arena, `reports/server-cost/stress-before.json`)
| per track (every 0.5 s, one tick) | 30 units | 200 units |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| whole track with a client | **12.6 ms** | **47.6 ms** |
| HUD model | 2.4 | 15.3 (units' data 10.5, misc 3.4) |
| 3D terrain | 6.0 | 6.8 |
| 3D things | 0.0 | 4.0 |
| server part (care 3.7, skills 4.5, far units 3.6 ...) | 4.2 | 21.5 |

### Plan (in order; each measured before/after, pictures and behaviour checked)
1. **Wall pass, exact fix (now):** inside one pass the ground can't change between floods (the pass never sleeps, and a
   walk is only taken up there with nobody on it), so a flood's answer holds for every tile it reached: the walls of
   one town share a few floods. Checked on every wall of the user's map: old and new answers compared wall by wall,
   and the rewritten flood against the original on the open tiles beside them.
2. **Active areas, Daggerfall style** (user, 21:5x: "do it how daggerfall online handles their server and their huge
   map"): an awake map of 16-tile chunks (WorldSave.dm's), refreshed every second: awake within the 3D view plus a
   margin round each connected player's camera, round each player's units, and round their workshops and banners.
   Outside it: the wall pass skips the walls; NPC wandering (`RandomWalk`/`GuardWalk`: gear look, step, target look)
   naps 2 s a round; gremlins' item hunts, poison plants and wild dragons' ticks rest. Hunger, bleeding and healing
   loops (40 s, 5 s) keep running everywhere: cheap, and nothing has to catch up. The awake area is bigger than
   anything a player can see (view, far units, fog sight), so nothing visible freezes; creatures walking in from the
   margin behave as now. Measured on the headless world (everything asleep), the user's game, and 200 units.
3. **New land without a burst** (user, 22:0x: "freezes when it loads new lands"): first measure a camera pan into
   unseen land (`--pan`, real client) for terrain rebuilds, far chunks, first-sight unit pictures and tile textures
   (built from sprite layers on the server: 4 facings x up to 5 frames x every gear layer), explore and fog marking.
   Fix by streaming ahead, Daggerfall style: build pictures and textures for things just outside the view a few per
   tick before they come into view, cache terrain per chunk, so arriving costs nothing extra. Page meshes are
   world-look's: I'll message before touching them.
4. **Per player at 200 units:** the HUD model's slow parts sent as changes or less often (positions still every
   tick), terrain cached per chunk, nothing built for units off screen.
5. **Memory (plan only, per the coordinator):** the Sky and Hell layers made when first entered (runtime `maxz` growth
   is verified, `tests/maxz_test.dm`), then regions loaded on demand (`planning/MMO_ARCHITECTURE.md` section 11).

**22:5x: plan step 1 is in game/** (`WallWalks.dm`: `rm_leak_memo` in `RemasterRegionLeaks`, set for the second loop of
`RemasterWallWalkPass` only; game/ compiles). Not built into the app: the equivalence run on every wall of the user's map
(`tests/wallpass_equiv.dm`, old against new per wall, and the rewritten flood against the original) waits until the
user has finished playing. Active areas (`Awake.dm`, written, not included yet) and the HUD selection lookup are in my
scratch copies until then.

### Toward 30,000 units (user, 22:4x: "i think we are going to have 30000 thousand units running around")
Read as about 30,000 creatures in one world, most far from any player. After plan steps 1–3. Per-unit costs below come
from Baseline 1 and 2 (each creature has its own sleeping DM loops: wandering every `Delay+1` ticks, bleeding every 5 s,
hunger, healing and tiredness every 40 s, a reset every 30 s, bed every 100 s). **Every capacity figure is an estimate**
until (a) measures it. "Fully active" means it thinks on every step as today. The budget is about 600 ms of each second
for creatures, leaving the rest for players' HUD and 3D, the network and GC pauses.

| step | what changes | fully active units one process can carry (estimate) | 30,000 in the world? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| today | everything everywhere, wall pass stalling | stalls already at 753 creatures (the wall pass), ~4,000 wild wanderers by CPU | no |
| 1 wall pass shared floods | no 0.1–1.1 s spikes | ~4,000 wild wanderers (~0.15 ms of DM a second each) or ~1,000 player units (~0.5 ms each plus their own loops) | no |
| 2 active areas | idle wild creatures far from players rest (one cheap check every ~2.4 s) | the same per awake area; a resting creature costs ~5 µs a second, so 30,000 resting ≈ 150 ms a second | **yes**, if no more than ~4,000 are awake at once; memory to be measured |
| (b) levels of detail | a coarse ring round the awake land: moves a chunk at a time, no paths, no look-rounds, thinks every few seconds; far groups (an army, a caravan, a village) folded into one record moving on the region map, members stored compactly off the map, unfolded when someone comes near | ~4,000 full + ~20,000 coarse; folded groups cost almost nothing (no loops, no engine entities) | yes, comfortably |
| (c) one brain per group | formations and bands decide as a group, members follow; shared routes (cached paths or flow fields) for many going the same way | groups of 30 cost about one unit's thinking plus cheap following: ~10,000 in groups | yes |
| (d) per-tick AI budget | each unit thinks on a staggered slot; work past ~60 ms carries over to the next tick | the same totals, but no tick overruns: slower thinking under load instead of stalls | yes |
| (e) spatial buckets | 16-tile cell lists for every "who is near" (target search, sweeps, wing mending, rot), no world-wide loops | ~1.5–2x on the above (target search is the biggest timed AI cost today) | yes |
| (f) native hot loops (plan only) | sight (`view`/`oview`), paths (A*), flood fills, target search moved into the engine (C#, patched OpenDream) | another ~5–10x on those parts; ~20,000 fully active | yes |
| (g) region shards (plan only) | MMO_ARCHITECTURE.md section 11: one DM server is one thread; regions on separate processes, a gateway hands players over | ×(number of processes) | yes, for 30,000 all active |

**(a) The stress world, first thing after steps 1–3:** a copy of the user's map with 30,000 creatures spread over it (NPC
towns, raiders, caravans, animals, armies) plus ~200 of the player's own; measure tick time, the worst tick, ticks over
100 ms and the physical footprint, with active areas on and off. It replaces the estimates above with numbers. Memory is
the open question: today the 4 million tiles already take ~3 GB (workstation GC), and every creature is a DM object
with its own sleeping procs and an engine entity; (b)'s folding is what keeps 30,000 inside a laptop's memory.

Order after 1–3: (a), then (e) (cheap, safe, helps everything), (d), (b), (c). (f) and (g) are plans for the
coordinator and the user to decide on.

### Toward 1,000,000 player units (user, 22:5x: "this is a persistent world, MMO i think we will see 1,000,000 million player units working and operating")
Read as a million player-owned units across the online world, working even while their owners are offline. Plan only.
Every figure is an **estimate** unless it says measured.

**The hard limit, honestly:** one DM server runs on one thread, through OpenDream's interpreter (a proc call costs
around a microsecond, a var read tens of nanoseconds). The measured cost is ~0.15 ms of DM a second for a wild
wanderer, ~0.5 ms for a player's unit with its owner watching. With ~600 ms a second for creatures, one process
carries ~1,000 watched player units fully active today, perhaps 3,000–5,000 after levels of detail, group brains and
spatial buckets ((b)–(e) above), and ~10,000 if the hot loops go native ((f)). A million running as real units at once
is out of reach for any number of interpreted processes we'd want to run. So almost all of them must not be units.

1. **Real units only where someone is watching.** A village or army is unfolded into real units only when an online
   player's camera or units are near it (active areas, plan step 2). With 1–5 % of the million watched at once, that's
   **10,000–50,000 awake player units**, plus the wild creatures round them. Everything else is (2).
2. **Unwatched and offline villages as economy records.** A village is one record: stock (food, wood, stone, ore, goods
   by kind and count), rates (what its jobs make and use per game hour, worked out from its people and workshops when
   it folds), its buildings by chunk, and its people as compact rows. It is caught up on contact or on a slow timer (the
   catch-up in `Away.dm`, which already replays up to 8 h at half pace in seconds, run in place as in
   MMO_ARCHITECTURE.md section 7). **A unit row:** id, name, race, sex, age, house and lineage ids, job, priority,
   home, ~25 stats and skills as small numbers, ~30 body-part states, mood, ~8 equipped-item ids, carried-item ids:
   **~300 bytes packed (~1 KB as JSON)**. A unit in today's save takes **~48 KB** (measured: the user's save, 3 units, 3 MB,
   most of it items with their pictures embedded). **A million rows: ~0.3 GB packed (~1 GB JSON), against ~48 GB plus
   items in today's format.** Items become rows too (kind, quality, count, holder: ~40 bytes each).
3. **Servers for the awake share.** At ~1,000 watched units per process today: 10–50 region processes for
   10,000–50,000 awake. At 3,000–5,000 after (b)–(e): **3–17**. At ~10,000 with native hot loops: **1–5**. Memory decides
   too: one 1000x1000x4 region costs ~3 GB (measured, workstation GC), so a 16 GB machine holds ~4 regions; regions
   with nobody in them are unloaded (MMO_ARCHITECTURE.md section 11), and their villages live on as records.
4. **Persistence in a database per region**, not savefiles. Today `SaveUnits()` rewrites every connected player's whole
   save (`M.Write`: every var of the player, every unit, every item with its picture) and the whole world save (5.9 MB,
   measured) every ~16 minutes, in one tick. Instead: tables for unit rows, item rows, building rows, changed tiles per
   16-tile chunk (WorldSave.dm's diff) and village records, written as changes (dirty rows every few seconds), in
   SQLite per region process or one shared Postgres. Pictures are never stored (they're made from the kind and gear).
5. **Time dilation** (EVE Online): an overloaded region slows its own game clock instead of freezing. The engine
   already slows the simulation when it falls behind (`GameLoop.cs` caps the backlog at 5 ticks), but in lurches. A
   region would instead measure its tick cost every few seconds and lengthen `world.tick_lag` smoothly (down to, say,
   40 % speed), so every unit's step, swing and work slows evenly. Clients are told the factor so the glide (step gap
   in ms, already sent per row) and the HUD's "Time 70 %" match. Real-time things (`RemasterNow`, the away catch-up)
   don't dilate.

**What today's code would have to change for this:**
- The per-creature spawn loops (`StartAllProcs` in `Mobs.dm`: bleeding, healing, hunger, tiredness, bed, the walk
  loops) become one scheduler with a slot per unit. Folding, budgets and dilation need it.
- `Saves.dm` `SaveUnits()`/`LoadUnits()` and `WorldSave.dm` → database rows and fold/unfold conversions.
- `Settlement.dm`, `FoodSupply.dm`, `Care.dm`, the workshops' crafting: a record-mode economy model that is the
  authority for unwatched villages, with the same recipes and rates (one source of truth, or the two drift apart).
- Owners as keys, not object links (WorldSave.dm already stores keys); `RemasterTrack` runs only for online players,
  as now; offline realms are "sleeping realms" (MMO_ARCHITECTURE.md section 7).
- Regions: `world.maxz`/region loading, a gateway that moves a player's client between processes, region-keyed claims.
- What stays as it is: the rules themselves (combat, skills, crafting, the HUD and 3D view) run on real units in
  watched places exactly as today.

**Players' units are the world's people** (user, 23:0x: "these player units will operate as the npc's as well and
etc"). There's no separate NPC population. The workers, traders, caravans, guards and soldiers anyone meets are
player-owned units acting on their owners' standing orders, also while the owners are offline. Wild creatures (animals,
monsters, dragons) stay world-owned, and they're the ones that simply rest when unwatched (plan step 2). For the plan:
- **The record tier carries what a unit is told to do:** its job and priority (Settlement.dm), standing orders (the
  Board's standing orders, Board.dm), trade routes and caravans (Trade.dm), patrol routes (Patrol.dm), garrison posts
  and stances (Defense.dm), work areas (Zones.dm). A record does what those say at its village's rates. A caravan
  record moves along its route on the region map, and unfolds into real units where it passes through watched land.
- **Records acting on each other are settled in one place, in time order.** Trades at a market, tolls on a road, raids
  on a village: each is an event with an id and a game time. The region that holds the place where they meet resolves
  it (authority by location), and each side applies it once (the id makes a repeat harmless). Across regions, events
  travel as messages stamped with game time, and a region applies them in time order before it moves on. That way
  two offline realms never disagree about a trade, and a catch-up gives the same result however late it runs. A raid
  between two records is decided by a battle estimate from both sides' strength, gear and defences. If either side is
  watched when it happens, it's unfolded and fought for real instead.
- **One brain for every role**, so the number that matters most is **what one unit's thinking costs per second**:
  orders tick, job choice, care, skills, look-rounds and paths, per role. The stress world (a) will measure it by role
  (worker, trader, guard, soldier in a band); today's figure is ~0.5 ms a second for a watched player unit, including
  its owner's HUD and 3D share. Halving it doubles what every region process carries, so it comes before (f) and (g).

### Native route-finding (A*): the plan (2026-10-24, user: "Plan native route-finding (A*) in the engine first ... Then we decide")
**What it costs now** (`reports/server-cost/astar-200-tick-profile.log`: +200 Dwarves, all selected, a group move every 20 s,
real client; the machine was loaded, load 5–9, so times run high, the shares hold):
- `RemasterOrderPath` (Orders.dm): **22 searches a second, 7.1 ms each, ~157 ms of every second**, which is **96 % of the
  group move's per-unit cost** (`RemasterGroupApproach` 163 ms/s). A 203-unit order costs ~340 ms on top.
- Per search: 155 expansions on average, ~720 walkability checks (`RemasterWalkable`: ~30 % of the time). **20 % of
  searches run to the 512-expansion limit** (no way through, retried every 3 s).
- The other ~70 % is bookkeeping: each expansion scans the whole open list for the lowest score (assoc-list lookups,
  so it grows with the square of the search), plus the cost/parent/closed lists and building the path.

**Step 1, no engine change (exact):** the same search, cheaper.
- A heap ordered by (score, order of insertion), which picks the same tile the scan does today: the first lowest in
  insertion order.
- Each tile's walkability looked up once per search (the map can't change during one; nothing in it sleeps).
- Expected **~2.5–3x** on route search (7 → ~2.5 ms).
- Proof: the old proc kept as a reference in a test fixture, run against the new one on (a) every search of a 200-unit
  real-client run, replayed with the same arguments, and (b) thousands of random searches on the user's map (towns,
  forests, mountains, stairs, wall-walks; flyers, undead on holy grass, beasts with feet, group pass lists, bounds and
  partial). The pass condition is **identical paths tile for tile and the same `rm_path_partial`**.

**Step 2, native in the engine:** the whole search in C#.
- Code: `engine/path/RemasterPath.cs`, patched into the Remastered runtime by `tools/build_runtime.py` the way
  `RemasterClock.cs` already is. A global native proc, e.g. `rm_path(M, goal, reach, bounds, radius, partial, pass)`,
  declared in a Remastered-only copy of the compiler's `DMStandard/_Standard.dm`, so the Classic replica stays untouched.
- Walkability is ported to C#, rule for rule: density, stairs unless the goal, wall-walk room, chasm and sky for walkers,
  holy grass for the unholy, dense movables except its own beast feet and walking group-mates, flyers over everything
  (`RmFliesOver`). The DM procs get a "mirrored in engine/path" note.
- A switch (`rm_native_path`) and a **shadow mode** (`RM_PATH_VERIFY=1`): both run, any difference is logged.
- Proof: the Step 1 harness plus shadow mode through soaks and real-client runs; on by default only after **zero
  differences over tens of thousands of searches**.
- Expected: **~20–50x on route search** (estimate: C# heap and var reads against the interpreter's ~1 µs per call), so
  157 → ~5 ms/s at 200 units, a group move's per-unit cost 0.8 → ~0.05 ms, and a 203-unit order 340 → ~50 ms (the
  rest is slots and formation work).
- What it takes:
  - the .NET 10 SDK downloaded again (~200 MB; the old copy in /private/tmp is gone; the user's OK first);
  - confirming the in-repo OpenDream source (`standalone/opendream`) is the version the runtime is built from;
  - a runtime rebuild and app build by the coordinator;
  - two copies of the walkability rules to keep in step (the shadow mode and a check catch drift).
- Risk: an engine bug can crash the server, not just a proc; hence the switch, shadow mode and fallback to the DM search.

**After both:** route cost stops being the per-unit number that matters. For very large armies the next step is
algorithmic, not native: one flow field per destination for a whole group (no search per unit), and searches over
16-tile chunks first for long marches.

**Order proposed:** Step 1 now (hours, no engine, exact); measure; then Step 2 if the user wants the MMO-scale
headroom (it's the biggest per-unit cost for armies).

**Step 1 tried and reverted (08:3x).** A heap keyed by (score, order added), plus each tile's walkability asked once per
search. It gives the **same routes**: `tests/rmpath_equiv.dm` (old search verbatim against the new one, back to back in
one tick, on the user's map) ran **6,248 searches with 0 differences** (4,927 found a route, 2,665 partial, 675 flying,
754 with group pass lists, 1,245 bounded). But it was **slower: 4.48 ms a search against 4.19**. In OpenDream's interpreter
every list read and write has a fixed cost, so at these sizes (open lists of ~60 tiles) the heap's pushes and sifts cost
more than the scan they replace. Orders.dm is back to the original, byte for byte. Conclusion: route search can't be made
much cheaper in DM; the gain is in the engine (step 2). The fixture stays as step 2's proof harness.

### Native route-finding, step 2 built and proven (09:2x; `planning/ENGINE_PLAN.md`)
- In the engine: `engine/native/RmPath.cs` (the search), `RmWalk.cs` (walkability), `RmNative.cs` (binding). The game
  side: `game/Code/Remastered/Native.dm` (`rm_path` with a DM fallback, `RM_NATIVE_PATH` and the `RM_PATH_VERIFY`
  shadow mode); `Orders.dm`'s search, unchanged, is now `RemasterOrderPathDM`. **Off by default, and in no app build yet.**
- **Proof:** `tests/rmpath_equiv.dm` (the old search against the engine's, back to back on the user's map) found 4
  differences in ~35,000 searches. All came at the goal near the 512 limit, with walkability equal on every tile
  (`rm_walkable` compared 1,881–2,891 tiles each time). Cause: the game's `get_dist` gives **-1 for the same tile**
  (the compiler's `_Standard.dm`), and the engine used 0, so the goal lost a tie. Fixed. Since then: **18,792 random
  searches and 6,479 searches on real 200-unit group orders (shadow mode), 0 differences, no runtime errors.**
- **Speed:** a search 4.65 → **0.21 ms** (22x). 200 Dwarves with a group move every 20 s, headless, on the same machine:
  order processing 79 → **11 ms/s**, a unit's group move 0.40 → **0.04 ms**, a 200-unit order 221 → 116 ms, DM per tick
  15.0 → **7.3 ms**, ticks over 100 ms in 6 min **92 → 9**.
- **One thing before it can ship:** the rebuild uses the in-repo OpenDream source (a shallow clone at upstream 2e58532,
  "Fix several refcounting bugs (#2734)"), which is one upstream commit newer than what built the shipped engine.
  The names differ only in #2734's files (`DreamList`, `DMProc`, `DreamManager`). The rebuilt engine ran the user's
  world cleanly, but an engine that's the shipped one plus the route search only needs the parent commit
  (`git fetch --deepen=1`, the user's OK for the download).

2e58532 (upstream fixes #2723, #2734 over the 5b186c2 the old engine was built from; the user chose the newer one) +
the Classic patches + the clock + native route search, checked name for name to keep every custom part.
Compatibility, headless, 200 units: new engine + game/ → native search on by itself, order processing 16 ms/s, no errors;
old engine + game/ → DM search, 66 ms/s, no errors. Restore point: `restore-points/engine-before-native-path-20261024/`.

## Ramps, the Gather switch, block-by-block mountains (ramps-gather, 2026-10-24, the user's ask)

The user's report: a built ramp couldn't be climbed; single-click gathering got in the way; only two blocks of a
mountain could be mined. Their decisions, asked as we went (memory: two-block-mining, gather-toggle, mountain-walking-rules):
- **Gather switch:** a button in the quick dock beside Lethal, key **G**, **off by default**, saved per player
  (`Player.remaster_gather`). Off: a click on rock, a tree or a fishing spot walks there; the right-click menu's Mine here /
  Chop it / Fish here still work (`work3d`; `walk3d` for Walk here). On: single-click work as before. The hover says
  "Move · Gather is off (G to mine)". skin.dmf's G now runs `Remaster-Gather` (it ran the old `Coords` teleport prompt).
- **Every mountain tile is a stack of blocks, one a layer**, and a click mines **only the block pointed at**, holes left
  with rock above and below (`turf.remaster_holes`, saved). Reach: **three blocks up from the unit's feet** (blocks 0-2
  from the ground), two under them; higher blocks are mined from up on the mountain beside them. Units up top dig a column
  down a block an order (Dig down). The 3D draws each block as its own faceted stone (`v3rockStack`, surface rock only;
  underground keeps the old look): rounded corners, chipped seams, uneven layers, seam points shared so it closes up.
  The highlight outlines that one block (`rfStackMark`), cracks show on it.
- **Walking on the blocks:** units stand on the top of each tile's stack; same height free, **up one block only by a ramp**,
  hop down one, never two; climbing gear (or a climbing race, a flyer) climbs. Up on the mountain the DM route search keeps
  these heights (the engine's search stays for every other level: `Native.dm` skips it for SKY_LAYER), and `Move` refuses a
  step that breaks them.
- **Ramps are one tile**, carved from the menu (**Carve into a ramp**: the column's top block becomes a slope rising away from
  the carver, who stands a block lower beside it). At the ground a ramp is the way up (`WallWalks.dm` `RemasterStairsTo`),
  walked onto from its foot; off a one-block top or a ramp, a hop down. The old multi-tile "Carve a ramp up from here" is gone
  from the menu (steps stay). Why a ramp couldn't be climbed before: `v3pickTile` skipped ramp tiles, so a click on the
  slope hit the rock behind it and mined it (fixed: `v3rampFloor`).
- **Cutaway** follows a selected unit of yours under rock (in a tunnel, a hall or a pit), cut at its ceiling or just over its
  head; with none of yours in there the whole mountain shows. The rock fade itself is unchanged ("the fade is good").
- **One block of room, everywhere** (the user, afternoon: "it defaults to all movement at the top of the mountain stack"):
  units stand and walk in any one-block gap with a block under it, at any height inside the mountain (`remaster_feet`,
  `RemasterSpotsAt`, `RemasterLevelPathDM`); a click on a dug-out floor walks there (Gather off; on, it mines that block),

  period once the caller yields (spawn), as the old `spawn() while(1)` did (a wild unit got one early bed check before).

- polish/polish-combat 10-26 00:04: POLISH LANDED "combat-batch": Six proven combat polish fixes in one landing (one gate): (downed-card-status) A unit lying knocked out or bleeding out still read 'Fighting <foe>' (or its last order) on its card and the Company list, and a foe it brought down read 'Fight over' instead of 'Won against'; now the card says 'Knocked out' / 'Bleeding out' and a fallen foe counts as won. Display only; needs downed-out-of-fight (RmDownOut). (falls-shots-throws) Every fall can be saved, but a thrown weapon, an arrow to the heart or lungs, or a weapon move's effect (lightning, astral, smite) that brought a unit down killed it at once (its killer is named as text, so Falls.dm never saw a foe); now those fall dying for 60 s like a blow's; the arrow-to-the-heart line no longer says 'instantly killed'. (nonlethal-archers) An archer on Non-lethal, or one given a Capture order, walked up to its foe and stood beside it for good with its bow (a bow strikes no blow, and Non-lethal never shoots); now it takes up a carried blade or its fists for the fight, as one out of arrows does, and the bow again after it. (attack-card-lines) Attack orders' card lines: an archer read 'Casting at <foe>' / 'Closing in to cast at' for its bow's move and kept it while shooting plain arrows (now 'Shooting at' / 'Closing in to shoot at'); and a unit whose foe fell while others stood near ended on a bare 'Idle' (now 'Brought down <foe>', as a Non-lethal one's 'Knocked out <foe>'). Words only. (captive-post-blocked) 'Tie to that tree/post' could stall for good: when the leader already stood beside the spot but in the captive's way (or another captive did), neither moved and the captive was never tied; now, after three pulls that bring it no nearer, the leader steps round to the far side of the spot. (down-check-once) Speed: the fallen-foe check (downed-out-of-fight) looked for a standing foe once per fallen candidate; an attack-move, an attack box and a creature's target search now look once per search. - polish/hud-rework 10-26 14:16: POLISH LANDED "hud-weapon-walk-swing": The owner (10-27): the weapons in the front view needs to animate dynamicly with the walking cycle; needs to be more dynamic looking; the weapons tips need to move towards center a little; the sword hilt is not on hand / it was just the sword was to low. A carried weapon now swings with the stride on a spring (lags the fist a little, overshoots a touch, settles when the walk stops; barely breathes standing), out and in seen from the front or back, forward and back seen from the side; the shield sways less the other way. Seen from the front its tip leans a little in toward the body's middle but stops short of the face (across the eyes its inner edge stays outside the head; where the walk frame's fist already holds it over the face it leans no further in). The longsword and rune sword sit 3 art pixels higher, so the grip is across the fist and the guard above it (before, the grip and pommel hung below the hand). Fighting and working keep their own poses. Pixel-art 3D gear only (gear3d.js). Files: art/gear3d/gear3d.js, game/Interface/gear3d.js. Gate compile+jscheck+hudjoin+combat PASS. Restore point restore-points/before-polish-hud-weapon-walk-swing-20261027-141639. Not built yet (goes in the next batched build).
- polish/hud-rework 10-26 14:17: POLISH LANDED "hud-3d-sharp-buffer": The owner (10-27): is there a way to make it less blurry from the camera angle if we are zoomed out a little; i want it look clean and detailed from zoom out to zoom in, we can fix performance in a different way. The 3D view drew into a buffer of the window's size before the HUD zoom, so with an Auto HUD size above 1 (or a larger HUD size chosen in Settings) it rendered 1/zoom of the screen's pixels and the window stretched it (soft); under 1 it rendered more than the screen (GPU for nothing). It now always renders at the screen's own pixels (full screen on the 1920x1200 screen held 60 fps there, 16.7-18 ms frames). - polish/hud-rework 10-26 14:17: POLISH LANDED "hud-3d-defined-pixels": The owner (10-27): no smooth but defined; i want it pixel to be smooth ... for the sprites or the units; make the pixel sprites in game be defined, no blur please. Pixel-art pictures in the 3D view (units, 3D gear, things) are drawn defined: every art pixel a crisp block, only its edge blended over at most one screen pixel at every zoom (filtered, premultiplied textures; the shader keeps the blocks), the outline smoothed by the view's multisampling (alpha to coverage, still depth-sorted). Nearest sampling gave uneven doubled pixels between zoom steps and dropped pixels further out. - polish/hud-rework 10-26 14:51: POLISH LANDED "hud-armed-walk": The owner (10-27): we need a new animation for when they have weapons held. A unit holding a weapon drawn in 3D now walks with that arm at its side, gripping, while its legs and other arm walk: every body sheet (80 Races64 sheets) gains an Armed state, its standing frame's right arm on its two walk frames (moved with the body's step, the walking arm's place filled from the sheet's own armless frame), and every right-arm armour piece (208 Gear64 sheets) an armed state the same way; nothing redrawn, every pixel the sheet's own (armed_walk.py). The server uses them for units holding a 3D weapon (Gear3D.dm RmG3Armed, View3D.dm Remaster3DLayers) and the page holds the weapon at the kept hand (gear3d.js, the anchors' armed steps). Before, the weapon hand swung across the body on every other step, taking the weapon over the chest and face. - polish/move-walk 10-26 15:50: POLISH LANDED "batch-walk-own-pace+walk-keep-route+walk-park-list+walk-stuck-flags": [walk-own-pace] Workers walked one tile per orders pass, so the bigger the village the slower they walked (2,000 workers: 0.5-0.75 tiles a second); now a job's own task (automatic orders) and a delivery step on along their route at the unit's own pace (its Delay, owner call A), the orders pass still doing the work and any new route. | [walk-keep-route] Every re-click dropped each unit's route and searched a new one, so spam-clicking a big group cost a route search per unit per click; now a re-click that gives a unit the same spot or slot (a move), or the same foe or attack-move spot, keeps the route it is on (owner call D). | [walk-park-list] The parked-unit sweep copied its whole list (8-42k entries at 2,000 workers) every 4 ticks and stopped for good if one call failed; now a unit has one entry at most, the list is compacted in place in the same order, and the next sweep is booked before the work (S2; same units set off at the same ticks). | [walk-stuck-flags] An error in a big group's first steps left the first-step drain marked running for good (every later order queued all but its first 2 units for ever), and a hand-out that died stayed in the ledger; now a failed first step is caught and the drain goes on, a drain silent for 2 s is started again, and dead hand-outs are dropped (S2b). - polish/move-walk 10-26 16:02: POLISH LANDED "walk-own-pace-floor": With own pace (call A) a job's walk and a delivery stepped at the unit's Delay, 25% faster than an ordered move (30 tiles in 120 ticks against 150); now they keep an ordered move's pace (never faster than RM_ORDER_STEP off a road, roads still speed them up), so workers are never faster than before, only no longer slowed by the village. - polish/step-cost 10-26 17:32: POLISH LANDED "step-merge-chains": Every unit step ran the Move chain's 7 pieces and the ground's Enter chain's 5 as 12 procs, each calling the next with a fresh copy of its arguments (arglist(args)), and the Move chain's bottom called Move() a second time to reach the parent type's; now each chain is one proc (mob/Monsters/Move, turf/grounds/Enter), the same steps in the same order with the same early stops and results, the parent's Move called straight from it, the profile's "creature move" around the same part. Nothing a player sees changes; a stone golem's own Move no longer needs to let the chain's second call through. - polish/step-cost 10-26 17:44: POLISH LANDED "step-skip-scans": Every unit step looked through the tile it stepped into for a door (the ground's Enter) and for a great beast's feet (Move), and called RmBeastLegsMangled for every unit; now each tile counts the placed doors and the beast feet on it (kept where doors are made, placed, deleted and once a second for any moved some other way; feet as they are set down, taken up and deleted), the looks run only where a tile counts one, and the legs are looked at only for dragons, spiders and golems (the proc gave 0 for anyone else). - polish/step-cost 10-26 17:56: POLISH LANDED "step-ground-timer": Every step of every unit ran the 2006 ground code (temperature, sunlight, a dragon's element points); now a step only counts, and about a second after a unit's first step (its own beat on the unit clock, spread over the second, only for units that walked) one run does it all for the tile the unit stands on then: each step's warmth or cold (frostbite and heat strokes at the same steps), a point of warmth back per step on grass and floors, a dragon's poison, fire, sand and ice points per step, and the sun once. What differs: the effects come up to a second after the steps, and all of a second's steps count as the tile the unit ends on (a step in and out of sunlight inside a second no longer burns a vampire or drains a svartalfar; one into it starts the burn up to a second later; mixed snow and grass inside a second counts as the last tile). Putting out a burning unit in water, falls from the sky or into a chasm and stairs stay on the step. rm_ground_timer = 0 puts it back. - polish/polish-lead 10-26 12:07: POLISH LANDED "death-once": Owner 10-28: "Death animation loop". (1) A dead unit's death act (deaths.js rdDie: a sway, then the crumple) was taken over by a guard or swing timed before it fell (skills.js skAct: one act a unit, the new one clears the old one's then): it swayed till the 4.5 s safety fall, or stood for good once its death was handed to its body. The dead now start no act but their death. (2) Its body could reach the page before its death hit and was then counted as an older body: shown under the doll, which stood up to act the death over it and fell again. Bodies first seen under 2.5 s ago count as its own. Same edits in art/gear3d (game.js, skills.js, deaths.js) and the installed game/Interface/gear3d.js. Filmed: m1 8 deaths, sway held to the safety fall in 4. (3) A knock or a blow's flinch timed before it fell (a swing's opt.knock, its last flinch) moved its fallen doll again: the dead take no flinch or knock (ragdoll.js rdStart). (4) Its death act takes its doll a frame or two after starting; a body arriving in between got the death with no doll (shown flat) and the doll later fell beside it: not handed to the body for its first 1.5 s. (5) A death act whose unit's doll could not act (knocked flying, down) was dropped and the doll stood till the safety fall: it now falls as it is. The page kept only the last 40 deaths, so in a big fight older ones were dropped while their doll still stood, upright for good: it now keeps 400, and past that the oldest fall as they go (a doll lookup once a frame instead of a search per death). A kill by a thrown javelin or axe now falls like an arrow's, also when the throw can't play. The hit flash stays, but a new hit no longer throws away every unit's kept drawing; only a unit flashing right now draws afresh. - polish/polish-lead 10-26 19:26: POLISH LANDED "public-guards": public-guards: what a player may ask of a public server (RM_PUBLIC=1, tools/public_host.py; owner 10-31: "Mac +
Tailscale, locked down"). After host-lock, the permission audit of every client entry point found:
- the world's difficulty could be changed by any signed-in player, announced to everyone;
- the old private messages (mob/Topic PM, PPM) went around the guest block, the mute (PPM) and the word list;
- the 2006 admin grants by address (Login.dm, Restart.dm) would hand every browser player the admin verbs and GM if
  they ever matched (every browser shares the proxy's address), and GM opens the create/edit links;
- anyone could force a whole-world save every 30 s (a spike each time);
- a vote's choice was taken unchecked (a bad one throws in the count).
On a public server: the difficulty is for Admins (the admin panel's owner/admin), private messages follow the chat rules
and the word list, no admin by address or by world.host, no create/edit links at all (the admin panel instead), and the
world saves itself. Solo play and Host for friends are unchanged, except that private messages go through the word list
(empty unless an Admin fills it) and a vote's choice must be one of its answers.
